messages:
anya: heads-up — noticed a regression on canary: short sequences (<=32) are routing to Triton and latency is ~15% worse than CUTLASS path.
sam: is this the new priority-ladder change from last week? I thought we biased triton for longer batches only.
anya: that's what I expected too. logs show the router picked Triton because of the priority ladder score: \"arch_score + batch_score + heuristic_bonus\". batch_score was low but heuristic_bonus seems high.
liang: can you paste the exact decision payload? the router emits a json blob when choosing a kernel.
anya: pasted below (sanitized):
```
{"model":"gpt-small","seq_len":16,"batch":8,"hw":"h100","arch_score":0.6,"batch_score":0.2,"heuristic_bonus":0.7,"final_score_triton":1.5,"final_score_cutlass":1.3}
```
sam: aha — heuristic_bonus 0.7 is the culprit. that's the new seq-length-aware multiplier we added for cold-kv paths.
matt: why would seq-length-aware multiplier favor Triton on short seqs? it was supposed to favor CUTLASS for small sequence, small batch microkernels.
liang: looks like the multiplier logic is inverted for kv_hot=false path. bug in the sign. quick diff:
```
- multiplier = (seqlen < 32) ? +0.7 : -0.3
+ multiplier = (seqlen < 32) ? -0.7 : +0.3
```
matt: oof. that would flip the ladder.
anya: confirmed by local repro: flipping sign brings median latency down 12% for seq<=32, p50 from 17ms -> 15ms.
perf-bot: small-run profile attached: cpu: router 8%, triton-infer 68%, cutlass-infer 45% (note: percentages are sample-time overlapping). :chart_with_upwards_trend:
sam: aside from the sign bug we should consider hysteresis — we saw oscillation when traffic mixes seq32 and seq256. kernel-switch churn increases latency.
liang: agree. propose two quick fixes: (1) flip sign to restore intended bias, (2) add 30s hysteresis per model+hw combo to prevent flip-flop.
matt: + implement a minimum score delta of 0.15 before switching routes so tiny telemetry noise doesn't trigger a switch.
anya: I'll open a PR for the sign fix + tests, add unit for multiplier semantics.
sam: can you also add an e2e canary that forces mixed seqs to catch oscillation? maybe a small ramp test.
anya: will add a canary job and alert if kernel route changes >20% in 5m window.
infra-bot: deploy canary to staging scheduled at 2026-03-18T02:00Z. tag: canary/priority-ladder-fix
matt: one more thing — KV cache cold-starts still bias heuristic_bonus because we used a naive cold_penalty. we should base penalty on kv_hit_rate rather than boolean.
liang: good call. i'll prototype a kv_hit_rate smoothing window (exp decay 30s) and feed that into the ladder.
sam: timeline: sign fix + unit tests today, canary tomorrow, kv_hit smoothing next sprint. sound ok?
anya: yep. I'll link the PR here once ready.
sam: thanks. saved us from a slow regression in prod. :+1:
perf-bot: perf diff (after sign flip, staging canary): median latency -11.4%, p95 -8.2%, tokens/sec +6.1%\n
